newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian Hansapank eyes more expansion.
newsitem.headline: Estonian Hansapank eyes more expansion.

text.p: Estonia's Hansapank, already the largest bank in the Baltic states, wants to spread its wings further in the region and the rest of eastern Europe, bank chairman Hannes Tamjaerv said on Wednesday.
Hansapank, with assets at the end of November of 5.3 billion kroons ($426.4 million), has already expanded into neighbouring Latvia, where it bought a bank and set up a subsidiary, Hansabank Latvija.
"We are in Latvia and more and more we are thinking about eastern (European) markets," Tamjaerv told Reuters in an interview.
"That does not mean rushing to be physically present but inviting Russian and Ukrainian business to the bank," he added.
Hansapank in November recorded its highest monthly profit, notching up income of 30.1 million kroons for a total so far in the year of 181.4 million kroons.
Tamjaerv said Hansapank had some 27 percent of the market.
"We are clearly close to the limit that we should have in one market but our growth potential is larger," he said.
"So we have to look for growth business either in other areas or in other geographical areas," Tamjaerv added.
After Latvia, Tamjaerv said that third Baltic state Lithuania was a definite area for expansion.
"We have decided to be a regional bank so clearly Lithuania is one target," he said.
But Tamjaerv said that no decisions on expansion had been made and that all the alternatives were being looked at.
Lithuania was the latest of the Baltic states to suffer a bank crisis at the end of last year and the bank sector is still going through a restructuring.
Poland's Kredyt Bank recently became the first foreign bank to get a licence to operate there.
Tamjaerv said that the Estonian bank market would probably see further consolidation as the number of banks was too big. But Hansapank was unlikely to take part in the process, he said.
"We can say that Hansapank has had to give answers to that type of idea (on mergers) but we have so far avoided everything," he said.
"In Estonia, Hansapank will not take part in any mergers or acquisitions," Tamjaerv added.
Estonia currently has 15 banks, including a branch of Finland's Merita.
